title: Build a word from invented parts
observableEvidence: Uses a root or affix to predict spelling or meaning.
prompt: The invented base grast means "to sort". Its spelling never changes when parts are added. Choose from these parts: prefixes re- (again), pre- (before), un- (not); suffixes -able (can be done), -ful (full of), -ness (state of). Build the one word that means "can be sorted again". Write it as one word with no hyphen.
solutionRepresentation: regrastable. "Again" is carried by re-, the base grast means to sort, and "can be done" is carried by -able, so the parts in order are re + grast + able. The base keeps its spelling, so nothing is dropped or doubled.
solutionMethod: Map each part of the target meaning to one affix, then join prefix, base and suffix in order.

deterministicValidator.equivalenceNotes: Spelling is letter-exact after case folding and trailing-punctuation removal; hyphens, apostrophes, spaces and diacritics are significant. The hyphenated form re-grastable is rejected because the prompt asks for one word with no hyphen.

hintSteps.prompt: Split the target meaning into its pieces: one piece about repeating, one about sorting, and one about being possible.
hintSteps.question: Which part from the list carries each piece of the meaning?

hintSteps.prompt: Prefixes go before the base and suffixes go after it. The base keeps its spelling exactly.
hintSteps.question: In what order do your three parts go?

hintSteps.prompt: Example with a different invented base: if plom means "to fold", then "the state of being folded before" is built as pre + plom + ness, written as one word.
hintSteps.question: Build the word for "can be sorted again" the same way. What is it?
